questions.q: What do we call the technique where a poet uses the same word or phrase multiple times to emphasize a point or make the reader laugh?
questions.a: It is called repetition. A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing it with rhyme, which involves sound, or word play, which involves meaning, rather than the act of repeating the actual text.

questions.q: If a poem uses the words "cat" and "hat" at the end of two lines, what device is the poet using? Explain why this makes the poem feel "light."
questions.a: The poet is using rhyme. This creates a musical or bouncy quality, which makes the poem feel playful rather than like a serious textbook passage. A wrong answer indicates the student does not understand how sound patterns affect the mood of a poem.

questions.q: Look at this line: "The baker was a kneady person because he always needed dough." Identify the word play (pun) and explain the double meaning of "kneady/needy" or "dough."
questions.a: The word play is on "kneady" (sounds like "needy") and "dough" (means both bread mixture and money). The student must link the baker's job to these double meanings. A wrong answer shows an inability to distinguish between standard definitions and clever word associations.

questions.q: Analyze this: "He ran fast, he ran far, he ran until he hit a star." Why does the author repeat the phrase "he ran"?
questions.a: The author repeats "he ran" to show the character's exhaustion or to create a comedic, panting rhythm. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks it is just a "mistake" or an accident, ignoring the deliberate nature of poetic craft.

questions.q: Evaluate this statement: "Rhyme is the most important part of every poem." Do you agree? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, because while rhyme creates music, humor often comes from word play or the surprise of repetition. A wrong answer shows the student believes all poems must rhyme, failing to recognize that devices serve different purposes.

questions.q: Create a one-line phrase using word play about a gardener.
questions.a: Example: "The gardener was outstanding because he stood out in his field." A poor answer would be a simple sentence without a double meaning, showing the student did not grasp the "play" part of word play.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Poetic devices are creative tools used by poets to make language more ______, musical, or humorous.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever noticed how a song gets stuck in your head because it keeps ______ a catchy chorus?
What is Poetic devices? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Poetic devices are creative tools used by poets to make language more interesting, musical, or humorous.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Poetic devices?
questions.a: Students often think "rhyme" just means any two words that sound vaguely similar, like "cat" and "car," or they think "repetition" must happen in every single line.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify examples of repetition, rhyme, and word play in a short verse and explain why the poet chose these specific tools to create humor.
